title: Learner 01 | Day 144: State machines and invariant checks
body:
## Goal

State machines and invariant checks

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/specializations/learner_01/core/state.py`

**Method/unit:** `transition_capability`

**Why here:** This is inside your owned AI/ML capability and the named layer. Model/data SDK details stay in adapters, rules in core, and commands/results in experience. It plugs into the same shared project architecture as other capabilities.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Denied cannot transition directly to saved; repeated save is safe; version conflict returns a clear outcome.

**Boundaries:** Keep the change inside the owned capability and preserve accepted behavior.

## Research hints

1. Research **State machines and invariant checks**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.python.org State machines and invariant checks`; use [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** Why bind an approval to a hash of the action payload?

**Review with @bitsnbyt3s:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
